result:
Added a paragraph to the hand-edits section of `docs/design/09-art-direction.md`, right after the part that explains why the unsigned guide gets no automatic amendments.

It records what reading your Neighbour edit turned up: every stroke you made was an erasure — 53 pixels at her feet across thirteen of the sixteen frames, no colour added, changed or removed, and each one moved the silhouette. The guide has no rule to hold that against. It fixes the ramps, the coloured outlines, the contrast between the world and the things worth touching, and the hues held back for overlays, and says nothing about where a sprite stops.

Two things I checked while writing it. Every generated sheet in the build stops hard — across all 51 of them, not one pixel is partly transparent — so the current behaviour is what the image pipeline happens to produce, not a choice anybody made. And the fourth look in the session list, more detail per surface, is described as "softer edges"; whether a soft edge may be a half-transparent pixel or has to be another step of the ramp is the same question, so answering it once settles both. The paragraph says so, and says this is for the session rather than an amendment.

check.summary: The paragraph landed where asked and every number in it matches the Neighbour edit ledger (53 pixels erased across 13 of 16 frames, all silhouette, all at her feet) and the 51 sheets on disk; the only thing to watch is that the hard-edge-everywhere claim came from the worker's own scan, which I could not re-run in this sandbox.

findings.what: The 'not one partly transparent pixel across all 51 sheets' claim was measured by the worker, not re-checked here; sheet count and ledger figures are confirmed, the alpha scan is not.
findings.fix: Before commit, run a one-line alpha scan over assets/sprites/generated/*.png and confirm zero partial values; if any appear, soften the sentence to name the exception.

findings.what: The neighbour sheet is not pipeline output — CREDITS.md records it as a palette remap of characters.png — so 'what the image pipeline happens to produce' is true of the folder in general but not of the very sheet the paragraph is about.
findings.fix: Optional: say 'what the pipeline and the remaps made from it happen to produce', or leave as is; the point about no rule having been chosen still stands.

recommend.question: Should the edge question reach the look session with pictures made in advance, or just be raised in the room?
recommend.answer: Make the two plates before the session and put the question on the card.
recommend.why: You would be ruling on a difference of a few pixels, which only shows itself on screen at real size.
recommend.instead: Leave the paragraph in the chapter and raise it verbally on the day — costs nothing now, but risks the session ending without an answer.
